body:
Thanks for the suggestion. We looked into all four tools:

HTA is built for distributed training analysis (multi-rank communication overlap, idle time). AutoKernel profiles a single model on one GPU so most of HTA's value doesn't apply here.

tlparse analyzes torch.compile logs. AutoKernel writes raw Triton/CUDA kernels and doesn't use torch.compile, so this is a different optimization path entirely.

mosaic analyzes memory usage. AutoKernel optimizes kernel throughput, not memory. Tangential to what we do.

trace-blame has some relevance for source-level attribution but our profiler already ranks kernels by GPU time which is exactly what the agent needs.

That said, we added opt-in flags for all of them (--export-trace, --memory-snapshot, --torch-compile-log) in case anyone finds them useful for debugging. They don't change the core workflow but they're there if you want them.

Hey Sayak, thanks for reaching out. We'd be interested in collaborating.

We added an export_hf.py tool that extracts CUDA source from our optimized kernels and generates the HF Kernels project structure (build.toml, torch_binding.cpp, __init__.py). It handles both CUDA C++ and Triton backends.

One thing we realized: the export generates the source layout but actually publishing to the Hub requires the full Nix build pipeline to cross-compile for all PyTorch/CUDA/ABI combinations. Our tool gets you to the starting line but not across it without kernel-builder and Nix.

Would love your team's help bridging that gap. If there's a simpler path to get kernels on the Hub (or if kernel-builder can be run as a service), that would make the integration much more practical for our users.

The code is live on main if you want to take a look: https://github.com/RightNow-AI/autokernel/blob/main/export_hf.py

Cc: @danieldk

Would collaborating on Slack be more useful? If so, I can create a shared channel.

Great work! May I also suggest looking at [nsight-python](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nsight-python) as a library for computing additional metrics? `nsight-python` runs [ncu](https://developer.nvidia.com/nsight-compute) to extract metrics.

## ✅ Verified on AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950 / CDNA4)

Tested end-to-end on **8x MI350X** (ROCm 7.2, PyTorch 2.10.0+rocm7.0, Triton 3.6.0):

### GPU Detection
```
gpu_name: AMD Instinct MI350X VF
gpu_sm_count: 256
gpu_memory_gb: 287.6
gpu_peak_tflops_fp16: 2300.0
gpu_peak_tflops_bf16: 2300.0
gpu_peak_bandwidth_gb_s: 8000.0
gpu_l2_cache_mb: 256.0
gpu_compute_capability: 9.5
```

GPU correctly identified via `gcnArchName: gfx950` → matched `"MI350X"` in `_KNOWN_GPUS`.

### Correctness
| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| Smoke test | ✅ PASS |
| FP16 shape sweep (10/10) | ✅ PASS |
| BF16 shape sweep (10/10) | ✅ PASS |
| FP32 shape sweep (7/10) | ⚠️ 3 fail (xlarge/deep_k/llm_mlp — tight atol, expected) |
| Numerical stability | ✅ PASS |
| Determinism | ✅ PASS |
| Edge cases | ✅ PASS |

### Performance (starter kernel, not optimized)
```
size            kernel_us   pytorch_us    speedup     tflops    %peak
------------------------------------------------------------------
tiny                 6.72         9.91     1.473x      0.624     0.0%
small               13.22         9.76     0.738x     20.298     0.9%
large               48.13        32.15     0.668x    356.930    15.5%
xlarge             323.68       129.86     0.401x    424.614    18.5%
llm_mlp            908.00       452.45     0.498x    406.791    17.7%
```

PyTorch baseline xlarge BF16: **956.5 TFLOPS** (41.6% of 2300 TFLOPS peak).

### Environment
- ROCm 7.2.0, PyTorch 2.10.0+rocm7.0, Triton 3.6.0
- Native gfx950 support (no `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION` needed)
- `torch.cuda.get_device_properties()` returns `gcnArchName: gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-`

Previously also verified on MI300X (gfx942, ROCm 6.3, PyTorch 2.9) — see PR description.

Closing this PR — the AMD Instinct GPU support changes (MI300X/MI325X/MI350X/MI355X detection via gcnArchName, GPU specs database, ROCm fallback paths) have already been incorporated into upstream main (commits 2465857, 7aa87ce). Thanks for merging the AMD support! 🎉
Updated `export_hf.py` for HF Kernels compatibility. Continuing on Slack.
